summary: Vidhushekhara Bhattacharya worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He held posts as a Pandit and collation supervisor at Visva-Bharati University (attested 1929–1944) and as Asutosh Professor of Sanskrit (Rtd.) at the University of Calcutta (attested 1941–1943).

Vidya Dehejia specializes in Indology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at St. Xavier's College, Newnham College, and the University of Cambridge (PhD ~1968), she served at Columbia University from 1982, becoming Barbara Stoler Miller Professor of Indian Art in 2002.

Vidya Niwas Mishra was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya and at Allahabad and Gorakhpur universities. He served as Professor of Linguistics at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1968–1989) and as vice-chancellor of Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith.
Vijaya Indra Suri worked in the fields of Indology and religious studies. Attested in 1933 as the successor to Vijaya Dharma Suri, he founded the Prakrit Text Society.
Vijayalakshmi Mani works in Indology and history and archaeology. Attested in 2026, she studied as a PhD scholar at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under doctoral supervisor V. Yamuna Devi.

Vilhelm Thomsen worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After completing his PhD at the University of Copenhagen in 1869, he served there as Privatdozent, associate professor, and full Professor from 1887 to 1913.

Vimla Karnatak works in Indology and philosophy. She studied under Gajanan Shastri Musalgaonkar and served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit at Banaras Hindu University (attested 2000).

Vinay Lal is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Johns Hopkins University (~1987–1992), he became Professor in the Department of History and Asian American Studies at the University of California, Los Angeles, around 1993.

Vincenc Lesný worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Charles University and under Josef Zubatý and Moriz Winternitz, later serving on the Charles University Faculty of Arts from ~1924 to 1952.

Vincent Arthur Smith worked in history, archaeology, and Indology, earning a doctorate from Trinity College Dublin. He served in the Indian Civil Service (1871–1900) as Commissioner of Gorakhpur and later curated the Indian Institute at Oxford University (~1910–1920).

Vincent Breugem specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Lucia Dolce, attended Taisho, Kyoto, and Hanazono universities, earned an MA and PhD at Leiden University, and served there as a research fellow (attested 2012).

Vincent Eltschinger works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate under Tom Tillemans at the University of Lausanne and his habilitation at Vienna, later becoming Directeur d’études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 2015.

Vincent Goossaert works in sinology and religious studies. After studying under Kristofer Schipper (~1993–1997), he worked at the CNRS (~1998–2012) and became Professor of Daoist History at the École Pratique des Hautes Études around 2012.

Vincent Lefèvre specializes in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the École Nationale des Chartes, Sorbonne Nouvelle University, and under Bruno Dagens, and has served as a curator at the Guimet Museum.

Vincent Tournier specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under Cristina Scherrer-Schaub, Seishi Karashima, and at EPHE, later holding positions at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities, and University of Tokyo.

Vincenzo Vergiani specializes in Indology and linguistics and studied under Raffaele Torella. At the University of Cambridge, he became Professor of Sanskrit around 2009 and headed a South Asian manuscript research project from ~2011 to 2014.
Virendra Kumar Varma is an Indologist and linguist who completed his traditional studies under Ramnath Dixit and Gopal Chandra Mishra.
Virendra Kumar Verma is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied under Ramanatha Dikshita and Gopal Chandra Mishra.

Virendra Nath Misra worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Lucknow (~1953–1957) and Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1958–1961), later serving as Director of Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1993–2000).

Vishnu Sitaram Sukthankar was an Indologist who completed his doctorate under Heinrich Lüders at Humboldt University of Berlin. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1915–1919) and became General Editor of the Mahabharata Critical Edition at BORI in 1925.
